source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 20 September 1946, p. 3 ("Nominations for county and rural councils: twenty-nine nominations for twenty-three Antrim seats"); Belfast News-Letter, 4 October 1946, p. 3 ("County and rural councils: results to-day"); Belfast News-Letter, 21 September 1946, p. 3 ("One withdrawal in Antrim: contests in five divisions")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: twenty-nine nominations for 23 seats; after Joseph Craig's withdrawal in Ballygomartin, five divisions were contested and 18 members were returned unopposed, one of them (Portrush) without any nomination.

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council on the 23 county electoral divisions; nominations received on 19 September 1946, withdrawals to 20 September, and the day of election was Thursday 3 October 1946 (official notice, Belfast News-Letter, 6 September 1946, p. 2). Polling took place on 3 October ('Polling took place ... yesterday', Belfast News-Letter, 4 October 1946, p. 3) and the count was held on 4 October. No party labels were printed. Added from reports of the new council's meetings early in the term, each division inferred from the previous return: Portrush. Returned unopposed.
